who: Warren I. Cohen, historian of American foreign relations, Michigan State University; PhD University of Washington, 1962.

evidence.says: UMBC identifies Warren I. Cohen as an American diplomatic historian specializing in American-East Asian relations, with a Washington PhD and prior employment at Michigan State before joining UMBC in 1993.
The career entry places Cohen at Michigan State from 1963, promoted to associate professor in 1967 and professor in 1971; it dates his Washington PhD to 1962.
The candidate's LC authority identifies Cohen, Warren I.; its source notes connect him to Michigan State and to UMBC, and identify his work Lyndon Johnson Confronts the World.

notes: The candidate's full name, diplomatic-history field and Michigan State career agree with the listed 1971-1978 dissertations.

who: Beth Barton Schweiger, historian of early America at the University of Arkansas from 2000; PhD University of Virginia, 1994.

evidence.says: LC explicitly equates Beth Schweiger with Beth Barton Schweiger; its university-source note gives a Virginia PhD in 1994, arrival at Arkansas in 2000, and specialization in early American social and cultural history.
Arkansas's record for Justin Randolph Gage's 2015 history PhD, Intertribal Communication, Literacy, and the Spread of the Ghost Dance, names Schweiger, Beth as advisor/mentor.

The 2019-2020 department newsletter uses both Beth Barton Schweiger and Beth Schweiger in its account of Chelsea Hodge; Schweiger directed Hodge's master's thesis and served on her dissertation committee, chaired by Michael Pierce.

notes: The authority's explicit name equivalence and Gage dissertation confirm the identity. Hodge's committee role should not be treated as proof that Schweiger chaired that dissertation.

who: William G. Shade, historian of nineteenth-century American politics and society at Lehigh University; PhD Wayne State University, 1966.

evidence.says: Brown's November 2018 notice says William G. Shade joined Lehigh in 1966; its September/October 2000 entry reports his retirement and describes his nineteenth-century American political and social history scholarship.
Lehigh's faculty and emeriti list identifies William G. Shade as professor emeritus of history and records his Wayne State PhD, 1966.
The candidate's LC authority is Shade, William G.; its source note identifies him as an associate professor of history at Lehigh and editor of Pennsylvania History.

notes: The full-name authority and Lehigh career through 2000 cover the listed 1977-1998 supervision period.

notes: The item explicitly includes the unaccented name. Institution, tenure during 2010-2015 and research fields agree with the listed dissertations.

who: David J. Weber, historian of the Southwest, Mexico and borderlands at Southern Methodist University, 1976-2010; PhD in Latin American history, University of New Mexico.

evidence.says: SMU identifies David J. Weber as a Southwest and Mexico historian, faculty member from 1976 until his teaching retirement in spring 2010, founding Clements Center director and mentor in its history PhD program; he earned his Latin American history PhD at New Mexico.

The candidate's LC authority identifies David J. Weber, author of The Mexican Frontier, and records that he was founding director of the Clements Center for Southwest Studies at Southern Methodist University.

notes: Full name, Clements affiliation, specialization and employment through 2010 agree with the listed 2007-2010 dissertations.

who: Marilyn J. Westerkamp, historian of early America, gender and religion at UC Santa Cruz; PhD University of Pennsylvania.

evidence.says: The UCSC directory identifies Marilyn J Westerkamp as a history professor, records a University of Pennsylvania PhD, and lists early American cultural and religious history among her research interests.
The UC repository identifies Marilyn J. Westerkamp as advisor and committee chair of Benjamin Michael Pietrenka's 2017 UCSC history dissertation on Moravian identities and religious radicalism.
Amy Hart's June 2019 UCSC history dissertation, Life After Community: The Communitarian Women Who Transformed Nineteenth-Century American Society, names Professor Marilyn Westerkamp as chair.
The candidate's LC authority identifies Marilyn J. Westerkamp as a UCSC history professor and author of Triumph of the Laity, Women and Religion in Early America and The Passion of Anne Hutchinson.

notes: The dissertations connect both name forms to the listed students; the Pennsylvania PhD matches own_phd. Pietrenka's repository title differs from the AHA title but has the same student, institution, year and subject.
